'''Ivan Georgiev Petrov''' ({{langx|bg|Иван Георгиев Петров}}; born 6 September 1949) is a Bulgarian-American [[physicist]] specializing in [[thin films]], [[surface science]], and methods of [[Characterization (materials science)|characterization]] of materials. His research and scientific contributions have been described as having an "enormous impact on the hard-coatings community".<ref name="special">{{cite journal |last1=Stübera |first1=Michael|last2=Hultman|first2=Lars|last3=Matthews |first3=Allan |title=Special Issue of Surface and Coatings Technology on 25 Years of TiAlN Hard Coatings in Research and Industry | journal=Surface & Coatings Technology | volume=257 | pages=1–2 | year=2014 |url=http://www.bgimages.org/papers/SCT_SpecialIssu2014.pdf | doi=10.1016/j.surfcoat.2014.08.060 |author-link2=Lars Hultman|author-link3=Allan Matthews}}</ref> Petrov was the president of the [[American Vacuum Society]] for 2015.

==Biography==
Ivan Petrov was born in 1949 in [[Shumen]], Bulgaria.<ref name="who">{{cite journal|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|date=2007|title=Ivan Petrov|url=https://archive.org/details/whoswhoinamerica00kare/page/3532|url-access=subscription|journal=Who's Who in America|publisher=Marquis Who's Who|publication-place=New Providence, NJ|volume=61|page=[https://archive.org/details/whoswhoinamerica00kare/page/3532 3532]|isbn=978-0-8379-7006-6|issn=0083-9396|access-date=26 January 2020}}</ref> For high school, he attended the [[English Language School "Geo Milev" (Ruse)|English Language School Geo Milev]] in [[Ruse, Bulgaria|Ruse]], graduating in 1968. He studied physics at [[Sofia University]] where he earned a [[Master of Science|MSc]] in 1974. He earned his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in physics from the Institute of Electronics at the [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]] in 1986, after which he became an associate professor until 1989.<ref name="who"/>

In 1989, he moved to the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] in collaboration with professor [[J. E. Greene]], serving initially as a visiting professor. From 1998 until 2010, he was an adjunct professor in the department of materials science and engineering, simultaneously serving as the director of the Center for Microanalysis of Materials at the [[UIUC Engineering Campus#Materials Research Laboratory|Seitz Materials Research Laboratory (MRL)]].<ref name="who"/> From 1998 to the present, he is a principal research scientist at the MRL.

Between 2000 and 2012, Petrov was an honorary visiting professor of Surface Engineering at the Materials and Engineering Research Institute of [[Sheffield Hallam University]] in England.<ref name="who"/> Since 2010 he is an adjunct professor in the department of physics, chemistry and biology (IFM) at [[Linköping University]]<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.liu.se/personal/ifm/tunnf/ivape26?l=sv&sc=true |title=Ivan Petrov: Adjungerad professor |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=liu.se |publisher=Linköping University |language=Swedish |access-date=27 January 2020}}</ref> in Sweden, where he was awarded an [[Honorary degree|honoris causa]] degree in 2009.

He was elected chair of the surface engineering division of the [[International Union for Vacuum Science, Technique and Applications]], serving terms from 2007 to 2022.

In 2014, he was elected as president of the [[American Vacuum Society]] for 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.avs.org/About/Governance/Past-Presidents |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200128221949/https://www.avs.org/About/Governance/Past-Presidents |url-status=dead |archive-date=28 January 2020 |title=Present & Past Presidents |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2020 |website=avs.org |publisher=American Vacuum Society |access-date=27 January 2020 }}</ref>

==Research==

Petrov's research elucidated the ways to obtain high-quality thin films, at low substrate temperatures, from refractory materials, such as [[Atomic layer deposition#Transition-metal nitrides|transition metal nitrides]], through the use of high-fluxes of low-energy ions.<ref>{{cite journal | author1=I. Petrov|author2=P. B. Barna|author3=L. Hultman|author4=J. E. Greene|author-link3=Lars Hultman |author-link4=J. E. Greene | title=Microstructural evolution during film growth  | journal= Journal of Vacuum Science & Technology A | volume=A21 | issue=5  | pages=117–128 | year=2003 | doi=10.1116/1.1601610 |bibcode=2003JVSTA..21S.117P| doi-access=free}}</ref>

He co-authored the seminal papers on [[High-power impulse magnetron sputtering]] (HIPIMS) which demonstrated that this technique produces highly ionized metal fluxes and opened additional ways to manipulate films properties.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Vladimir Kouznetsov |author2=Karol Macák |author3=Jochen M. Schneider |author4=Ulf Helmersson |author5=Ivan Petrov | title=A novel pulsed magnetron sputter technique utilizing very high target power densities | journal=Surface and Coatings Technology | volume=122 | issue=2–3 | pages=290–293 | year=1999 | doi=10.1016/S0257-8972(99)00292-3 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author=Karol Macák |author2=Vladimir Kouznetsov |author3=Jochen Schneider |author4=Ulf Helmersson |author5=Ivan Petrov | title=Ionized sputter deposition using an extremely high plasma density pulsed magnetron discharge | journal= Journal of Vacuum Science & Technology A | volume=A18 | issue=4 | pages=1533–1537 | year=2000 | doi=10.1116/1.582380 | bibcode=2000JVSTA..18.1533M }}</ref>

Petrov was one of the principal investigators of the [[Transmission Electron Aberration-Corrected Microscope]] (TEAM) project from 2000 to 2009.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kisielowski |first1=C. |last2=Freitag |first2=B. |last3=Bischoff |first3=M. |last4=van Lin |first4=H. |last5=Lazar |first5=S. |last6=Knippels |first6=G. |last7=Tiemeijer |first7=P. |last8=van der Stam |first8=M. |last9=von Harrach |first9=S. |last10=Stekelenburg |first10=M. |last11=Haider |first11=M. |last12=Uhlemann |first12=S. |last13=Müller |first13=H. |last14=Hartel|first14=P. |last15=Kabius|first15=B. |last16=Miller|first16=D. |last17=Petrov|first17=I. |last18=Olson|first18=E.A. |last19=Donchev|first19=T. |last20=Kenik |first20=E.A.|display-authors=1 |date=October 2008 |title=Detection of Single Atoms and Buried Defects in Three Dimensions by Aberration-Corrected Electron Microscope with 0.5-Å Information Limit |journal=Microscopy and Microanalysis |volume=14 |issue=5 |pages=469–477 |bibcode=2008MiMic..14..469K |doi=10.1017/S1431927608080902 |pmid=18793491|s2cid=12689183 }}</ref>

He is an author on over 300 publications, which have been cited more than 22,000 times by other scholars.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=WpbZnwsAAAAJ |title=Ivan Petrov |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2022 |website=Google Scholar |access-date=28 September 2022}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
* 1996: Sustained Excellence in Research Award ([[United States Department of Energy|U.S. Department of Energy]])<ref name="who"/>
* 2001: Named as a [[Fellow]] of the [[American Vacuum Society]] (AVS)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://avs.org/Awards-Recognition/Society-Honors/Fellow-of-the-Society |title=Society Honors: Fellow of the Society |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2019 |website=avs.org |publisher=American Vacuum Society |access-date=27 January 2020 |archive-date=14 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160314034305/http://avs.org/Awards-Recognition/Society-Honors/Fellow-of-the-Society |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* 2009: R&D100 Award by R&D Magazine as a co-inventor of the TEAM electron microscopy stage<ref>{{cite web |url=http://mrl.illinois.edu/news/team-stage-recognized-2009-rd-100-awards |title=TEAM Stage Recognized in 2009 R&D 100 Awards |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=20 July 2009 |website=mrl.illinois.edu |publisher=Illinois Materials Research Laboratory|access-date=27 January 2020 }}</ref>
* 2009: Bunshah Award and Honorary Lecture from AVS for "development of a detailed understanding of the role of low-energy ion-irradiation on microstructural and texture evolution during transition metal nitride layer growth"<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.avs-ased.org/wp/?page_id=46 | title=Bunshah Award Past Recipients | date=2019|website=avs.ased.org|publisher=American Vacuum Society, Advanced Surface Engineering Division |access-date=27 January 2020}}</ref>
* 2013: John A. Thornton Memorial Award and honorary lecture from AVS for "seminal contributions in determining the role of low-energy ion/surface interactions for controlling microstructure evolution during low-temperature growth of transition-metal nitride layers"<ref>{{cite web |url=https://avs.org/Awards-Recognition/Professional-Awards/John-A-Thornton-Memorial-Award-Lecture |title=Professional Awards: John A. Thornton Memorial Award/Lecture |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2019 |website=avs.org |publisher=American Vacuum Society |access-date=27 January 2020 |archive-date=29 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200129202549/https://avs.org/Awards-Recognition/Professional-Awards/John-A-Thornton-Memorial-Award-Lecture |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* 2014: the journal ''Surface & Coatings Technology'' dedicated a special issue to Petrov, recognizing him as "a true pioneer in the science and technology of hard coatings" and that "his papers have been, and still are, must-reads for both newcomers to the field and experienced colleagues"<ref name="special"/>
* 2014: Academician Emil Djakov Award from the Institute of Electronics, [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]] for Petrov's "prolific research in the field of radiophysics, physical and quantum electronics and his contribution to raising the prestige and development of international cooperation of the Institute of Electronics at the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences"<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ie-bas.org/Awards.htm#award40 |title= Academician Emil Djakov Institute of Electronics, Bulgarian Academy of Sciences: Awards |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=15 May 2015 |website=ie-bas.org |publisher=Bulgarian Academy of Sciences |access-date=27 January 2020}}</ref> 
* 2017: Lifetime Achievement Award and honorary lecture from the Taiwan Association for Coatings and Thin Film Technology{{Citation needed|date=January 2020}}
* 2019: Lifetime AVS Honorary Membership<ref>{{cite web |url=https://avs.org/Awards-Recognition/Society-Honors/Honorary |title=Society Honors: Honorary Membership |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2019 |website=avs.org |publisher=American Vacuum Society |access-date=27 January 2020 |archive-date=29 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200129202610/https://avs.org/Awards-Recognition/Society-Honors/Honorary |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Personal life==

Ivan Petrov is the son of [[:bg:Георги Петров (агроном)|Georgi Petrov]], a Bulgarian agronomy professor, and Russanka Petrova. He is married to Vania Petrova, and they have a son Georgi.<ref name="who"/>
